problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{16}∼N(-3,{8}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $16$ from a normal population, calculate $P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.5).$ *Hint: Value tables of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.04\,$$\,0.05\,$$\,0.06\,$

worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(-3,\frac{{8}^{2}}{16}) \\  & ∼N(-3,4).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.5).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.5) & =1-P(|\overset{―}{X}|<0.5) \\  & =1-P(-0.5<\overset{―}{X}<0.5) \\  & =1-P(\frac{-0.5-(-3)}{\sqrt{4}}<Z<\frac{0.5-(-3)}{\sqrt{4}}) \\  & =1-P(1.25<Z<1.75) \\  & =1-(Φ(1.75)-Φ(1.25)) \\  & =1+Φ(1.25)-Φ(1.75)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.25) & =0.8944, \\ Φ(1.75) & =0.9599.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.5) & =1+Φ(1.25)-Φ(1.75) \\  & =1+0.8944-0.9599 \\  & =0.9345.\end{aligned}
$$
